newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian teachers protest wage delays.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian teachers protest wage delays.

text.p: Up to 15,000 teachers rallied in Kiev on Sunday to demand months of back pay in a protest drawing attention to a $1.5 billion wage arrears crisis which has left millions of Ukrainian government workers unpaid.
"The education system is suffering and there is no future," said Kiev teacher Olena Istomina. "A teacher no longer has reason to go to work."

Teachers and university professors arrived from across Ukraine to mass peacefully in the central parts of Kiev, joining smaller protests of about 2,000 teachers taking place in several other Ukrainian cities.
"Don't promise us heaven, just give us our pay," said one of the many signs at the protest.
"The government has brought us to our knees, and we have become slaves," said another teacher from a Kiev elementary school.
Many teachers have stopped working as the government has failed to fulfill promises to clear wage arrears also owed to doctors, civil servants, miners, students and pensioners.

Average monthly pay in Ukraine stands at about $80 a month, and small protests and strikes demanding backpay have become a frequent occurrence in Ukraine. About 200,000 coal miners in the eastern Donbass coal regions struck in July.
